concept.name: ARIMA model
concept.definition: An integrated autoregressive moving-average model, ARIMA(p,d,q), that extends the ARMA model to non-stationary series by differencing the data d times and then fitting autoregressive (order p) and moving-average (order q) terms to the differenced series. It is the core of the Box-Jenkins identification-estimation-validation methodology.
concept.intuition: Many real series wander with a trend or unit root, so you difference them until they look stationary, model the differences with an ARMA model, and sum forecasts back up to the original scale.
concept.mechanics: Identification uses the ACF and PACF of the (possibly differenced) series to choose p, d, q; parameters are estimated by (conditional) maximum likelihood; residuals are checked for remaining autocorrelation. Forecasts of the differenced series are integrated (cumulatively summed) to produce level forecasts.
concept.formula: phi(B)(1-B)^d X_t = c + theta(B) A_t, where B is the backshift operator, phi(B) = 1 - phi_1 B - ... - phi_p B^p the AR polynomial, theta(B) = 1 - theta_1 B - ... - theta_q B^q the MA polynomial, and A_t white noise.
concept.failure_modes: The differencing choice is fragile: under-differencing leaves a unit root and spurious inference, while over-differencing induces artificial moving-average structure and inflates forecast variance. ARIMA also assumes a stable linear process, so structural breaks degrade forecasts.
concept.misconceptions: That ARIMA models trending or seasonal series directly: the 'I' handles only stochastic trends via differencing, and periodic structure needs seasonal terms or prior deseasonalizing. A good in-sample fit also does not imply genuine predictive content.
concept.example: Log prices of an equity index are close to a random walk, so an ARIMA(0,1,1) models the change in log price as a moving average of past forecast errors and integrates the forecasts back to price levels.

citations.source: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, Section 6.4.4.5 Box-Jenkins Models
